h1: Impact Ventures — Fintech Hero Section Design
tagline: “We shape digital products that define brands” — the whole hero section is composed around that line, down to the animation timings.
summary: Hero section reference for a fintech product — 700ms transitions, React and Tailwind CSS, Instrument Serif and cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1) easing.
about: Impact Ventures solves the hero section problem for a fintech product with a single captured brief. The page's own headline reads “We shape digital products that define brands”, and the composition is built around those exact words. The palette runs blue #2D64B0 underneath and white #C5D5DE for the type, and the type is Instrument Serif. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 640x472 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. Motion is confined to 700ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1). Use it as the reference when you are building a fintech product hero section and want a finished composition instead of a starting point.

layout.title: Navigation without a background
layout.body: A slim bar sits over the hero section with the wordmark on the left and the links set in Instrument Serif, so the composition reads as content first and chrome second. A mobile overlay takes over below the tablet breakpoint. The bar sits over the 640x472 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: Every measurement is written down
layout.body: The list stays short (700ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1) easing), which is why the whole system can be checked by hand. Values are quoted from the captured prompt rather than inferred, so they survive a re-render.

layout.title: The footer is a full composition
layout.body: Links are grouped into columns with the wordmark in its own block, which keeps a long footer readable instead of turning it into a list. The accent is reused on one footer action rather than across the whole band.

layout.title: One row, no drawers
layout.body: Give the wordmark no more room than its type needs. The reference was captured at 640x472.

motion.title: Hover, but sparingly
motion.body: Every interactive element does one thing (hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card), which is what keeps the states predictable. The states are drawn from the page's own palette rather than from a component default.

motion.title: Timing kept in the brief
motion.body: The brief fixes the transition value at 700ms, so a rebuild cannot substitute a slower default. Focus states are timed with the same value as hover, so keyboard and pointer feedback match. Fast state changes, no scroll timelines.

fonts.name: Instrument Serif

notes: Transitions are specified at 700ms, short enough that the page never feels like it is waiting for an animation.

editorial.title: What a fintech product gains here
editorial.body: Where a template fills the fold with modules, this hero section uses navigation, the stats row, the feature list, the background clip and the footer and stops. The difference shows in 700ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1) easing: nothing is padded to fill space. Impact Ventures states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: How Impact Ventures sequences the first read
editorial.body: Nothing here competes with the first decision. The page says it out loud: “We shape digital products that define brands”. The supporting material waits below the fold, and navigation, the stats row, the feature list, the background clip and the footer carry the top of the page alone. A fintech reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: How the hero section reflows
editorial.body: The narrow layout is designed, not inherited. the navigation collapses into a mobile menu at each width, so the hierarchy survives the reflow. Nothing important is dropped at narrow widths.

faq.question: Is the Impact Ventures prompt a finished spec or a starting point?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 4,400 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: How much of Impact Ventures depends on React and Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: Impact Ventures was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: What drives the motion in Impact Ventures?
faq.answer: The motion is specified at the same level of detail as the layout: state changes settle in the 700ms range on cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1). Port the composition first and the timings second, because they are easier to match once the layout holds.
